per section 1 below, same obligation already accepted for symphonia
(MPL-2.0) in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Using this unmodified file from
Dawsons' own proprietary code does not obligate open-sourcing Dawsons
itself — this is exactly the use case "Lesser"/"Library" GPL exists for,
distinct from the GPL/AGPL licenses this project has rejected elsewhere
(see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md's "Explicitly excluded" table) specifically
because those would have forced the whole program open.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

Can I use LAME in my commercial program?

Yes, you can, under the restrictions of the LGPL.  The easiest
way to do this is to:

1. Link to LAME as separate jar (lame.min.js or lame.all.js)

2. Fully acknowledge that you are using LAME, and give a link
   to our web site, lame.sourceforge.net

3. If you make modifications to LAME, you *must* release these
   these modifications back to the LAME project, under the LGPL.
